1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line spacing, though letter spacing appears default rather than especially generous.

2.why: No italics, no all-caps instructional text, and no dense text blocks appear on any screen; the uppercase string is the secret code itself, not an instruction.

3.why: Only desktop-width screenshots were provided; the single narrow centered column suggests the layout would reflow, but mobile rendering is not actually shown.

4.why: Instructions are one short sentence each (e.g., 'Choose manual entry and enter this setup secret:'), though terms like 'MFA enrolment' and 'browser console' are jargon.

5.why: The email and mobile fields are prefilled with example values, but the six-digit code field shows no example or placeholder of the expected input.

6.why: The longest text on any screen is two short lines, so the user never has to read a long block of text to proceed.

7.why: The 32-character secret is rendered as plain text that appears selectable, but there is no copy button and the test code is only available in the browser console.

8.why: The page explicitly instructs 'Choose manual entry and enter this setup secret:' and no QR code or equivalent alternative is shown on any screen.

9.why: The fields are standard text inputs, but no autofill behaviour or password-manager support is observable from the screenshots.

10.why: Each screen has a bold heading naming the step and one large blue primary button, though the persistent Logs panel adds competing content and there is no step indicator.

11.why: Every screen asks for exactly one main action ('Verify and continue', 'Set up authenticator app', 'Confirm code'), with only 'Log out' as a secondary option.

12.why: After each action the heading changes to the next step and the Logs panel states what happened ('Configured identity verification completed'), but success is confirmed only in the logs rather than the main content.

13.why: A wrong code produces an error with the entered value preserved and no lockout, so retry without penalty works, though there are no reveal/hide or re-request controls.

14.why: The only error message, 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.', does not blame the user but also does not identify the actual problem or a specific fix.

15.why: No countdown, timeout, or time-limit warning appears on any screen and failed codes can be retried, although the code is described as 'time-bound'.
